Title: FDS victims' families want full crash report released transparently
Article:
KUCHING: Families of the victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, want the full investigation report released transparently, without being concealed or politicised.
Nor Izzati Syamimi Suhaimi, wife of Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, said the crash had deeply affected all the victims' families, who were still waiting for a clear explanation of its cause.
"I do not know what to comment, but I hope the report will be released more transparently, without being concealed or politicised.
"The crash has had a huge impact on all of us," she said when contacted.
Muhammad Faiz Abdul Malek, husband of medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, said investigators had informed the families that the findings were preliminary.
He said the families had been told that the full investigation report could take between one and two years to complete.
"The investigation team said we could contact them if we needed to know anything.
"However, the findings we were informed of that day were only preliminary.
"This means the fully confirmed findings are not yet available," he said.
Meanwhile, Stephanie Essah Incham, wife of medical assistant Alexson Adit Henry, declined to comment on the latest developments in the investigation.
"Please give me some time to rest.
"I have just completed several matters with the Sarawak Health Department," she said.
The preliminary report on the Sept 8 crash involving a Bo-105 helicopter, released by the Air Accident Investigation Bureau today, said the safety investigation was ongoing and the available factual data remained preliminary.
The report found no faults with the helicopter's airframe, maintenance or pilot at this stage.
However, the helicopter's engines had been sent to the manufacturer's facility for further examination. The
investigation into the powerplant remains ongoing
, and any implications for the airworthiness of other engines of the same type have yet to be established.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Knife seized in investigation into woman's alleged murder
Article:
SEREMBAN: Police found a knife on a mattress in the master bedroom of a government agency officer's home, where she was allegedly murdered by her husband yesterday.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the weapon was found after the suspect himself pointed it out during an inspection at the scene.
"The knife is suspected to be linked to the incident and has been seized for further action and forensic examination," he said when contacted today.
In the incident about 7pm on Thursday, a man reportedly surrendered at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi police station in Sepang, claiming that he had killed his wife.
Alzafny said the cause of death of the 35-year-old victim had yet to be determined, as a post-mortem was scheduled for tomorrow.
However, he said an examination at the scene found stab wounds to the left side of the victim's abdomen and her right cheek.
He said preliminary investigations indicated that the incident was believed to have stemmed from marital discord.
"Based on initial questioning, an argument broke out after the victim expressed her intention to divorce the suspect and informed him that divorce proceedings had been initiated while he was serving a prison sentence.
"However, the exact date the divorce was filed is still being verified through the relevant official documents," he said.
Alzafny said the couple had been married for seven years and had two children, aged 6 and 5.

Title: Pearly–Thinaah break new ground in Denmark
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Women's pair Pearly Tan–M. Thinaah were made to work before reaching their first Denmark Open semi-final on Friday.
The world No. 5 came back from a game down to defeat India's world No. 18 Treesa Jolly–Gayatri Gopichand 14-21, 21-17, 21-11 in their quarter-final at the SJF Bank Arena.
The breakthrough saw Pearly–Thinaah surpass their previous best showing at the Super 750 tournament, a quarter-final appearance in 2024.
They will face sixth seeds Bao Li Jing-Cao Zi Han from China in the semi-finals.

Title: Jetour shifts gears from SUVs to global travel lifestyle
Article:
CHINESE automotive brand Jetour is expanding its push into the global travel lifestyle market, combining sport utility vehicles (SUVs), off-road technology and conservation initiatives under its "Travel+" strategy.
Founded in 2018, the brand has built its identity around box-style SUVs that combine everyday practicality with off-road capability and long-distance comfort.
Jetour said its cumulative global sales reached 2.56 million units as of September this year, with vehicles available in more than 100 countries and regions.
It also ranks first in box-style SUV sales in 13 countries, according to the company.
The brand will showcase its technology and travel-focused strategy at the 2026 Jetour Global Technology Experience Day, themed "Future Travel Starts Now", from Oct 20-23.
The event will bring international guests through urban areas, mountain terrain and wetlands to demonstrate the company's approach to combining vehicle technology with outdoor exploration and environmental conservation.
Jetour's product range is organised around its T-Series and G-Series, with the company seeking to expand its presence in established automotive markets, including Europe, Australia and New Zealand.
Its global expansion follows the strategy "In Somewhere, For Somewhere, Be Somewhere", which focuses on adapting its products and operations to different markets.
Beyond vehicle sales, Jetour is positioning "Travel+" as a broader lifestyle proposition built around exploration, philanthropy and culture.
On the technology front, the company highlights systems such as XWD fully automatic intelligent four-wheel drive, the GAIA all-terrain intelligent architecture and C-DM super hybrid technology.
These are intended to extend the vehicles' capabilities across different driving conditions while making off-road features accessible to a wider range of buyers.
The company is also linking its travel activities to wildlife conservation.
In Africa, it has partnered with Discovery and the Cheetah Conservation Fund on the "Return of the Cheetah" initiative.
In Malaysia, it has established philanthropic partnerships with TCS and Pulihara, while in Pakistan it launched the Markhor Conservation Programme to support wildlife and habitat protection.
The initiatives form part of Jetour's effort to associate travel with environmental responsibility, alongside its automotive business.
Jetour said it aims to make four-wheel-drive and hybrid technologies more accessible to families, broadening the appeal of off-road vehicles beyond specialist enthusiasts.
The strategy reflects its ambition to build a business around travel experiences as well as vehicle ownership, while expanding its international product range and customer ecosystem.
However, its ability to sustain global growth will depend on market-specific demand, competition and the execution of its expansion plans.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: When banking products converge, experience becomes the differentiator
Article:
OPEN the app of almost any bank in Asean, and you will find much the same thing: instant transfers, QR payments, rewards tabs and basic chatbots.
Features that once set a bank apart are now matched within months.
What customers remember is how quickly an account opens, what happens when a payment fails, and whether help is available when needed.
Unlike a product feature, experience depends on data, processes and people working as one.
Banks that treat it as a growth strategy rather than a service function will pull ahead.
Across Asean, core banking products - savings accounts, cards, loans and digital services look increasingly alike.
Twimbit's forthcoming Asean Banking Titans 2026 research benchmarking leading banks across the region finds that on core journeys such as account opening or moving money, top banks are separated by narrow margins.
Product and pricing still matter, but they no longer set banks apart.
Where banks do differ is in what surrounds the product.
Our research finds that digital capability is now the region's strongest foundation, whereas service - how a bank responds, resolves and recovers when something goes wrong - is where it is weakest.
Consistency is harder still. Leadership in account opening rarely carries over to transfers or app usability.
That moves customer experience (CX) beyond a service team or satisfaction score.
When CX shapes which bank customers choose, use and stay with, it becomes a growth strategy.
AI raises the stakes further. Customer-facing AI is increasingly shifting to act - completing steps across onboarding, card servicing, loan enquiries or disputes - moving from response to resolution.
Twimbit's latest AI-CX research reveals that close to US$10 billion was invested in AI for customer experience globally, and is expected to cross US$50 billion by 2030.
But adding AI does not guarantee a great experience.
An AI agent cannot resolve what the organisation has not made resolvable.
If data is fragmented, processes span multiple teams or ownership is unclear, customers still feel the friction.
The question is whether the bank is organised to let AI act usefully, safely and consistently.
The AI-CX research therefore assesses agentic AI maturity alongside orchestration and governance: an agent is only as good as the systems it can work across and the controls around it.
Once AI acts on a customer's behalf, trust becomes more concrete.
It is tested during unrecognised transactions, declined applications, or missing funds.
Our journey analysis shows key gaps - failed transfers often lack a clear explanation, minimal guidance on how to fix a failed identity check, and basic chatbots are slow to hand over to human agents.
Speed matters, but so do clarity, reassurance and accountability.
That makes fraud and scams a customer experience issue as much as a security one.
Explainability, guardrails and access to a person belong in the design from the start, while early governance gives banks the confidence to scale responsibly.
The goal is not maximum automation, but the right automation.
Routine, high-volume interactions are obvious candidates for AI. But complex or emotional moments require human judgement supported by AI insights to unify context and resolve the issue faster.
As banks plan for 2027, four questions deserve clear answers.
Which journeys should be redesigned rather than simply digitised? Where should AI act autonomously? What needs to change in data, processes and ownership?
And where will customers still expect human judgment?
Twimbit will release the findings from its "State of Asean Banking CX 2026" flagship report and recognise leaders in banking experience, AI experience, app experience, onboarding experience, most inclusive banking and digital banks on Oct 27.
*The writer is senior vice president of Twimbit.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Onn Hafiz calls Asean meeting as Johor records 53rd day of haze
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi has called for an emergency Asean meeting and stronger regional cooperation to tackle transboundary haze, as the state recorded its 53rd day of haze since Aug 25.
He said regional cooperation must be strengthened in fire prevention, hotspot monitoring and firefighting efforts to prevent further haze episodes.
The issue was raised at a state-level disaster coordination meeting, where Onn Hafiz warned that the prolonged haze posed a serious threat to public health and daily life.
He said data from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre showed 453 hotspots in Indonesia's Kalimantan and 153 in Sumatra, raising concerns over fires and smoke spreading across borders.
Pasir Gudang recorded an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 198, approaching the very unhealthy threshold of 201.
Larkin recorded an API reading of 196, followed by Pengerang (180), Kota Tinggi (171), Batu Pahat (170), Kluang (164), Tangkak (159) and Segamat (155).
All eight monitoring stations in Johor recorded unhealthy air quality, with PM2.5 identified as the dominant pollutant.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two TNB contractors suffer third-degree burns in Tebrau substation incident
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Two Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) contractors suffered third-degree burns after being electrocuted during maintenance work at a substation in Kangkar Tebrau.
The New Straits Times learnt that the victims, Malaysians aged 39 and 31, sustained the burns in the incident.
Both men received initial treatment from firefighters before being rushed to hospital.
The incident occurred around 6.10pm at the Kangkar Tebrau main intake substation in the Tebrau 4 Industrial Area.
It also triggered
power disruptions
in more than 10 residential areas across the city, including Taman Johor Jaya, Taman Molek, Adda Heights, Bandar Dato' Onn, Austin, Eko Flora, Cascadia, Kempas, Setia Tropika, Taman Gaya, Senai and Taman Pelangi Indah.
Johor Fire and Rescue Department operations commander Fadzil Yahya said firefighters arrived at the scene six minutes after receiving the emergency call.
He said eight firefighters were deployed to the scene and found both men had suffered electric shocks while carrying out maintenance work.
Operations ended at 6.45pm.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Loke: RTD to fully cooperate in probe into fatal Senawang crash
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Road Transport Department (JPJ) will cooperate with the police to ensure a thorough and transparent investigation into a crash that killed one of its personnel and seriously injured another near the Senawang exit on the North-South Expressway last night.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said action would be taken against any party found to have violated the law or committed misconduct.
"If there are any legal violations, misconduct, or negligence identified through the investigation, action will be taken against the responsible parties in accordance with the provisions of the law and regulations in force," he said in a statement.
Loke extended his condolences to the family of Negri Sembilan RTD Enforcement Assistant Grade KP2 Mohd Azrul Rashid Yaakub, who was killed in the accident while on duty.
"Azrul's passing is a great loss, particularly to his family and colleagues. His sacrifice and dedication in carrying out his duties for the safety of road users will always be appreciated," he said.
He also wished Motor Vehicle Examiner Grade AB2 Nor Amirudin Rameli, who was seriously injured in the crash, a speedy recovery.
Loke said RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli had visited the families of both officers this morning to convey his condolences and offer support.
The Transport Ministry and RTD would continue to look into the welfare and needs of the deceased's family and the injured officer, including providing appropriate assistance, he added.
The crash occurred around 10.50pm when RTD personnel were inspecting a lorry parked on the emergency lane at KM256 of the southbound North-South Expressway near the Senawang exit.
A lorry driver approaching from behind veered out of control and crashed into the RTD sport utility vehicle (SUV) and the lorry being inspected.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor Baru power outage: Substation fire in Tebrau disrupts electricity supply
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Firefighters are battling a blaze at an electrical substation in the Tebrau 4 Industrial Area in Jalan Kangkar Tebrau here, with several nearby areas experiencing power outages.
The Johor Fire and Rescue Department said it received an emergency call at 6.10pm, with firefighters from the Tebrau Fire and Rescue station arriving at the scene six minutes later.
Eight firefighters and a fire engine were deployed to tackle the blaze.
No casualties had been reported as of the latest update, while firefighting operations were still underway.
Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), in a statement, said the fire at the Kangkar Tebrau main intake substation had disrupted electricity supply to several areas in Johor Jaya.
"Our technical team has been deployed to the site and is working to restore power to affected consumers," the statement read.

Title: Cape EMS ties up with Taiwan's FIC Global unit
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Cape EMS Bhd has signed a memorandum of agreement (MoA) with Taiwan's FIC Global Inc unit Pro3C (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd to support the latter's expansion in Johor's artificial intelligence (AI) manufacturing supply chain.
The agreement, signed on Oct 16, positions Cape EMS as Pro3C's local strategic partner, providing manufacturing infrastructure, supply chain management, facilities and operational support.
The collaboration supports Cape's CEB 2.0 transformation, aimed at improving facility utilisation, generating recurring revenue and shifting its electronics manufacturing services (EMS) business towards higher-value manufacturing.
Pro3C's manufacturing facility at i-Park @ Senai Airport City, which was opened on Oct 15, represents a first-phase investment of about US$50 million.
The plant manufactures components for 800G, 1.6T and 3.2T high-speed optical transceivers used in AI infrastructure, high-performance computing and data centres.
Pro3C currently operates eight surface-mount technology production lines with about 530 employees.
It plans to increase capacity by 125 per cent to 18 lines by 2027, with potential expansion of its manufacturing floor space by up to four times.
FIC Global is targeting revenue of up to US$2 billion from its Johor operations in 2027, subject to customer demand.
Cape EMS group managing director and chief executive officer Christina Tee said the collaboration presented an opportunity to revitalise its EMS business and strengthen its position in advanced electronics manufacturing.
The MoA also provides for a potential subscription by Pro3C or its nominee for redeemable convertible preference shares in Cape EMS, subject to separate commercial terms and regulatory and shareholder approvals.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt supports efforts to strengthen Islamic scholarship, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government supports efforts to strengthen Islamic scholarship, research and intellectual discourse to contribute to national governance and the well-being of the ummah, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
In a post on X, Anwar said this after receiving a courtesy call today from a delegation from Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin International Islamic University (UniSIRAJ), led by its board chairman, Perlis Mufti Datuk Dr Mohd Asri Zainul Abidin.
"The meeting discussed the 2027-2030 Action Plan of the al-Qaradawi Institute of Thought (IPQ), which focuses on research, publications, talent development and strengthening scholarly networks," he said.
Anwar said the meeting also discussed a proposal to organise the International Seminar on al-Qaradawi Thought next year to broaden discourse on Islamic thought and contemporary national governance challenges.
In a separate post, Anwar said the government had always valued the contributions of community organisations committed to supporting the national development agenda, strengthening the spirit of togetherness and ensuring that the people's well-being remained a priority.
Anwar also met a delegation from the Malaysian Islamic Welfare and Dakwah Organisation (Pekida), led by its president, Datuk Mohd Foad Mat Isa.
He said the meeting was an opportunity to strengthen ties between the government and community organisations, and enhance cooperation in promoting national unity, harmony and public well-being.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China tells Trump's press secretary to visit 'more often' after toilet comments
Article:
BEIJING: Beijing told White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia on Friday to visit China "more often" after she said the country lacked "proper toilets" less than a week into her new post.
After years of intense rivalry between the United States and China over issues ranging from trade and technology to Taiwan and human rights, the US president's new spokesperson took the relationship between the two sides into uncharted territory.
Zacharia, who previously lived in China and is due to visit next month, recalled in an interview the perception in 2016 that China would soon overtake the United States.
"I remember this very distinctly, having just come from China, thinking, 'How is China the next country on the horizon? They don't even have proper toilets," she told right-wing influencer Jack Posobiec.
In response, China's foreign ministry on Friday suggested she might want to make another trip to the country.
"We welcome her to visit China more often when she has the opportunity," spokeswoman Mao Ning told reporters, suppressing a smile.
Trump has often spoken about his "great relationship" with Chinese President Xi Jinping, whom he has met twice this year, although ties remain strained.
Zacharia's remarks came just days after what many considered a questionable debut before the White House press corps, during which she appeared unable to answer basic questions and at one point referred to her husband as the president.
The 41-year-old is already under scrutiny over her legal credentials after giving an inconclusive answer about where she had passed the bar exam, a prerequisite for practising law in the United States.
The self-described lawyer lists herself as general counsel of a California-based conservative non-profit organisation. She has also said she previously worked at a law firm in Beijing.
Asked about her legal background on Thursday, she said she had registered to take the bar exam but was then "distracted and overwhelmed" by plans to move to China with her husband.
Zacharia said she did not retake the bar exam after returning to the United States because of the birth of her first child.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MBI Selangor subsidiaries form strategic alliance to explore dark fibre network 2.0
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Smartsel Sdn Bhd and Pengurusan Air Selangor Sdn Bhd (Air Selangor), key subsidiaries of Menteri Besar Selangor (Incorporation) (MBI Selangor), will explore the proposed Selangor Dark Fibre Network 2.0, which aims to leverage existing utility corridors to deploy high-capacity fibre networks.
The initiative aims to meet growing connectivity demand from telecommunications operators, data centres, cloud providers, artificial intelligence infrastructure and businesses.
The collaboration between the two subsidiaries was formalised today after the exchange of a memorandum of collaboration (MoC) at the MBI Pavilion during the Selangor International Business Summit (SIBS) 2026.
The partnership combines Air Selangor's water utility infrastructure with Smartsel's digital infrastructure and technology capabilities to develop digital connectivity and intelligent infrastructure across the state.
MBI Selangor group chief executive officer Datuk Ts Saipolyazan M Yusop said the collaboration aimed to translate group synergy into commercial opportunities and greater value for Selangor.
"We must move beyond the traditional mindset of operating as separate companies. We must begin to see ourselves as part of a larger ecosystem, where the assets of one company can create opportunities for another," he said in a statement.
The two companies will also explore smart water technologies, including fibre sensing, Internet of Things (IoT) and real-time monitoring, to strengthen pipeline surveillance, enable earlier leak detection and improve operational efficiency.
The companies will also further assess the potential use of selected elevated water tank and service reservoir sites for telecommunications infrastructure, distributed edge computing and modular data centres, subject to technical feasibility and operational requirements.
"The collaboration will also explore enterprise connectivity, managed information technology, cloud services and cybersecurity to support Air Selangor's digital transformation," the statement said.
Both companies intend to establish a joint working framework to evaluate priority initiatives, assess technical and commercial feasibility, and develop mutually agreed implementation roadmaps.
-- BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pasir Gudang blaze extinguished after 43 hours
Article:
PASIR GUDANG: A fire involving piles of timber and buoys in Jalan Muhibbah, Kampung Pasir Putih, here, was fully extinguished yesterday after nearly 43 hours of firefighting.
The blaze, which broke out at 10.04pm on Oct 14, engulfed 1.3935ha of open land before firefighters extinguished it at 4.47pm yesterday.
Johor Fire and Rescue Department operations commander Nazarudin Yusof said firefighters had contained 98 per cent of the blaze
by 8am yesterday
, covering about 148,000 sq ft, before continuing efforts to put out the remaining hotspots.
"By 4.47pm, 100 per cent of the fire had been extinguished, with no remaining area affected by the blaze," he said in a statement today.
A total of 19 firefighters took part in the operation, supported by 17 personnel from other agencies, including the police, Ulu Tiram Volunteer Fire Brigade, Malaysian Civil Defence Force and SWM Environment.
No casualties were reported.
Johor Fire and Rescue Department director Siti Rohani Nadir said witness accounts indicated that several men from a nearby village had
set fire to a pile of wood
to recover scrap metal, with the blaze believed to have spread to nearby fibreglass floats.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Families of children killed in Pakistan school roof collapse demand justice
Article:
PESHAWAR: The families of children killed when a school roof collapsed in northwest Pakistan called for "justice" on Friday, a day after more than 30 pupils and a teacher were crushed to death.
A woman teacher and 32 students, mostly younger than 14, died when the building collapsed in the city of Peshawar on Thursday morning.
"The parents of all these children must receive justice," tailor Muhammad Wahab, who lost his 11-year-old nephew Hammad in the accident, told AFP on Friday.
"I appeal to our rulers," he said, adding that Hammad had been "doing well in school" before the tragedy.
Dozens of people gathered outside the school on Friday to mourn the children killed in the collapse, which officials blamed on dilapidated infrastructure.
One grief-stricken father showed AFP a picture on his mobile phone of his young daughter, dressed in red and gold, who lost her life.
Another parent, Asadullah, said he had lost a son, a nephew and three other close relatives in the tragedy.
"The children were good students and often achieved top positions in their classes," he told AFP. "They happily went to school every day."
Residents and rescuers described chaotic scenes in the aftermath of Thursday's collapse, as people scrambled to pull children from beneath the rubble.
A man named Sohail told AFP that "everyone began screaming in panic" when his niece, who had escaped the building, arrived home to tell them it had collapsed.
"When I arrived at the scene, I saw around 10 to 15 children trapped beneath the rubble, with debris piled up to their necks. We quickly pulled them out," he said.
[[nid:1556979]]
School owner detained
Images released by emergency services showed rescue workers in high-visibility vests scrambling to move debris, rubble and dirt.
A senior official in Peshawar told AFP that initial reports suggested the roof collapse was due to "weak infrastructure".
"The school owner has been detained," the official said on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to speak to the media.
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif expressed "deep sorrow and grief over the loss of precious lives" in a post on X.
President Asif Ali Zardari described the roof collapse as a "heartbreaking tragedy".
Building collapses are common in Pakistan, largely due to poor safety standards and substandard construction materials in the South Asian nation of more than 240 million people.
In June, more than a dozen children were killed when a roof collapsed at a tutoring centre in the eastern city of Lahore.
In 2025, 27 people were killed and 10 injured when a five-storey building collapsed in the impoverished Lyari area of the southern city of Karachi.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: UM student who questioned Najib donations faces online harassment, threats
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Universiti Malaya (UM) student leader who questioned public donations to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak has faced online harassment and threats after videos of her remarks went viral.
Ummi Umairah Bakhit, 23, said she would not be intimidated by the attacks, adding that she believed it was her responsibility to challenge public perceptions, particularly among young people.
The Bachelor of Economics student stood by her remarks, saying corruption must remain part of the national conversation.
"After the video went viral, they took my photos from Instagram without my consent.
"Some of them also threatened me with expulsion from the university, harassed me, made comments about my physical appearance and much more," she said when contacted.
Ummi, who is also a member of the UM Student Union, said her questions were relevant as the forum had also focused on transformation.
She hoped her actions would encourage others to speak up without fear, participate in co-curricular activities and remain active in various fields.
"Corruption is also one of the important things if you want to build a nation, the same as climate change, artificial intelligence and education, like what the panellists discussed during the forum," she said.
Ummi said Deputy Higher Education Minister Adam Adli had checked on her and assured her that she would not be expelled or face disciplinary action.
She said the university had not taken any action against her, adding that claims of her impending expulsion had originated on social media.
Ummi raised the issue during a dialogue with former minister Khairy Jamaluddin, Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari and Johor Menteri Besar Datuk Onn Hafiz Ghazi at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur.
She questioned
public donations to Najib,
citing his legal cases linked to 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) and his conviction in the SRC International case.
"The stupidest thing I have watched in my entire life is people donating to our former prime minister, Najib Razak, someone who clearly has a worldwide corruption case, 1MDB, and is clearly linked to corruption," she said.
Ummi also raised the Tabung Haji controversy and sought the panellists' views on corruption and political accountability.
Her remarks have since gained traction on social media platforms, including TikTok and Instagram, where clips of the exchange have attracted likes and shares.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia ready to help Indonesia fight forest fires, says Zahid
Article:
TIANJIN (CHINA): Malaysia is ready to assist Indonesia in tackling widespread forest and land fires after President Prabowo Subianto agreed to accept offers of aid from neighbouring countries.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Malaysia welcomed Indonesia's willingness to receive foreign assistance and remained committed to helping its neighbour, in the spirit of friendship and strong bilateral ties.
"We are grateful to the Indonesian government and President Prabowo for being open to accepting foreign assistance to tackle the forest fires.
"Even though the help we have offered is small, Malaysia is prepared to send aid to assist our neighbour," he said, adding that Malaysia values ​ Prabowo's openness on the matter.
He was speaking shortly before departing China after concluding a five-day working visit.
Earlier, Indonesian Foreign Ministry official Arrmanatha Nasir said Prabowo had approved offers of assistance from neighbouring countries, with technical discussions under way to determine how the aid would be delivered.
However, he did not specify which countries had offered assistance or what form it would take.
Malaysia had previously offered to deploy a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 52 personnel to help Indonesia tackle the fires.
On Sept 19, Zahid said Prabowo had accepted the offer during a meeting the previous day in Hambalang, West Java.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia on track to exceed 2026 GDP growth forecast — Economists
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is on track to exceed the official full-year gross domestic product (GDP) growth expectation of 4.8 to 5.3 per cent after the economy expanded by 5.5 per cent in the first nine months of 2026, said economists.
The Finance Ministry, in its Economic Outlook 2027 report, has raised its 2026 real GDP growth projections to 4.8 to 5.3 per cent, up from 4.0 to 4.5 per cent in Budget 2026.
Prof Dr Yeah Kim Leng, director of the economic studies programme at the Jeffrey Cheah Institute of Sunway University, said the third-quarter (3Q) GDP expansion of 5.3 per cent affirms the economy's resilience despite continuing geopolitical uncertainty and persistent global oil shocks.
"With growth hitting 5.5 per cent in the first three quarters, the economy is on track to exceed the full-year official 4.8–5.3 per cent GDP growth expectation," he told Bernama.
Yeah said growth moderated slightly compared with the previous quarter but held up well against the challenging external backdrop of continuing geopolitical uncertainty and persistent global oil shocks.
"Encouragingly, the manufacturing sector picked up pace, indicating sustained export demand not only for high-value electronics and optical products but also resource-based chemicals, plastics and rubber products that have higher domestic value added," he added.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the latest GDP performance was a positive surprise, with growth potentially surprising on the upside against the prevailing projection of between 4.8 per cent and 5.3 per cent.
"At 5.3 per cent, the Malaysian economy is seen to be growing above its trend level of around 4.7 per cent," he said.
Mohd Afzanizam said positive appetite among foreign investors to invest in Malaysia, along with greater demand for the technology-related sector, helped sustain economic growth momentum.
Full employment also helped maintain steady consumer spending as inflation remained fairly contained, he added.
Earlier today, the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) announced in its advanced estimates report that Malaysia's economy expanded by 5.3 per cent in 3Q 2026, after registering 6.0 per cent growth in the preceding quarter, while for the first three quarters of 2026, the economy achieved growth of 5.5 per cent, higher than the 4.8 per cent recorded in 2025's corresponding period.
Domestic demand and E&E to sustain growth
Meanwhile, RHB Investment Bank Bhd (RHB IB) is maintaining its 2026 GDP growth projection at 5.4 per cent, with its autoregression and leading economic index models pointing to sustained growth momentum of 5.0–5.2 per cent in the second half of the year (2H 2026).
"Robust growth of 5.7 per cent in 1H 2026, together with today's 5.3 per cent growth reading, which was in line with our in-house expectation, reinforces our constructive outlook.
"Looking ahead, economic activity is expected to remain supported by resilient domestic demand and sustained strength in electrical and electronics (E&E) exports," it said in a research note today.
RHB IB said private consumption is projected to remain firm, underpinned by healthy labour market conditions, continued income growth and civil servant salary adjustments.
"Private investment should also remain resilient, driven by infrastructure projects, ongoing data centre developments and capacity expansion in manufacturing.
"Meanwhile, continued digitalisation, automation and favourable global demand should encourage further investment, particularly in manufacturing and information and communication technology," it said.
In a separate note, Kenanga Investment Bank Bhd has also maintained its full-year growth forecast at 5.3 per cent, although the stronger-than-expected advance estimate points to an upside risk to its forecast.
It said any revision would hinge on September's data and the full GDP release.
"Domestic demand should increasingly drive growth in the 2H 2026, backed by resilient consumer spending, strong services activity and continued investment in artificial intelligence (AI) and digital infrastructure.
"Implementation of approved projects, rising household incomes, and a firm labour market add further support," it said.
Kenanga said that manufacturing should remain a key driver on sustained E&E demand from AI and data centre expansion, although growth may slow as front-loading fades.
External risks remain, OPR hold expected
Mohd Afzanizam said the Malaysian economy remained fairly resilient despite external shocks, especially the ongoing war in Iran, which is likely to affect global supply chains and fuel costs.
He said proactive government measures, such as targeted fuel subsidies via MyKad since last year, along with efficiencies demonstrated by Petroliam Nasional Bhd in procuring fuel supplies beyond the Strait of Hormuz, had allowed the economy to operate almost seamlessly.
RHB IB, however, said geopolitical tensions in West Asia, commodity price volatility and shifting trade policies pose risks to the outlook.
"Prolonged tensions and elevated oil prices could raise production and transportation costs while dampening global demand," it said.
Separately, CIMB Treasury and Markets Research said the stronger third-quarter outturn points to a modest overshoot of its 5.0 per cent growth forecast for 2026, which would be revised after the full 3Q GDP release in November.
"Stronger external demand remains supportive of the manufacturing outlook, particularly in E&E, where manufacturers have reported longer order books," it said.
Despite the GDP upside, CIMB retained its expectation for Bank Negara Malaysia to hold the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent in November, given signs of moderating domestic activity and contained inflation.
RHB IB also expects the OPR to remain unchanged at 2.75 per cent at the November Monetary Policy Committee meeting, saying the current economic environment and inflation trajectory support a broadly stable policy outlook.
DOSM said the preliminary GDP, which provides a detailed and comprehensive analysis of economic performance for 3Q 2026, will be released on Nov 18, 2026.
-- BERNAMA

Title: Indian police detain 'cockroach' movement founder Dipke ahead of protest
Article:
NEW DELHI: Police detained Abhijeet Dipke, founder of India's 'Cockroach' movement, on Friday, according to live footage shared by his group, ahead of a protest he had called in the capital's central business district.
The rally was the latest in a series of demonstrations demanding the resignation of India's election chief.
The youth-led 'Cockroach Janta Party' (CJP), opposition groups and student organisations have held almost daily protests this month demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over a revision of voter lists that critics say favours Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).
More than 130 million voters were deleted during the revision, but the Election Commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters can re-enrol. The BJP has accused rivals of trying to undermine democracy by wrongly questioning legitimate electoral processes.
Dipke called Friday's protest in support of two CJP leaders who were detained and sent to jail this week for five days after demonstrating at a protest site in violation of a ban.
The group and left-wing student organisations had urged supporters to gather at Central Park in New Delhi's busy Connaught Place shopping and food district on Friday evening to wave and hoist the national flag.
Live video on CJP's Instagram account showed Dipke leaving a house and walking towards the street, where police officers stopped him and, after a brief argument, bundled him into a police car and drove away.
"We are detaining you right now," a police officer could be heard telling Dipke.
"I have not broken any law right now... how can you detain me," Dipke asked the officers as he was taken away.
There was no immediate comment from the police on the detention.
Earlier on Friday, police met Dipke and warned him against going ahead with the protest.

Title: Malaysian suspected of running RM7.2mil agarwood scam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian is suspected of masterminding an agarwood investment scam involving more than HK$14 million (RM7.2 million) that was uncovered by Hong Kong police on Wednesday.
The South China Morning Post reported that the man was among six people arrested in raids across Hong Kong. The other five suspects were Hong Kong residents.
The operation, codenamed "Shadow Net", was launched by the Hong Kong Police Commercial Crime Bureau after it received 21 reports from investors since September.
Commercial Crime Bureau Superintendent Allan Chu Ming-lun said most victims were aged between 52 and 82.
He said they had invested between HK$30,000 (RM15,565) and HK$1.9 million (RM985,800) in schemes offered by a Hong Kong-based company since 2017.
The company claimed to have offices in Malaysia, Singapore, New York and Hong Kong, as well as large agarwood plantations in Malaysia producing essential oils, tea and food.
"Key members of the syndicate took investors on visits to agarwood plantations in Malaysia to gain their confidence.
"The company also frequently organised investment seminars at its Hong Kong office, offering free tours and meals to encourage existing members to recruit new investors," he said as quoted by SCMP.
Investigations found that the company offered at least four investment schemes promising high returns.
Under one scheme, investors could buy an agarwood tree for HK$10,000 (RM5,194) in return for promised monthly payouts of HK$300 (RM156), equivalent to 36 per cent annually.
They were also promised a full refund after three years, while the monthly returns were recorded as reward points on the company's mobile application.
However, some investors began finding in 2024 that they could neither withdraw their returns nor recover their initial investments.
Chu said the company then used various excuses to delay payments and introduced new schemes to persuade investors to transfer their funds from earlier investments.
In 2025, it launched an intellectual property licensing scheme promising annual returns of up to 25 per cent. Investors unable to recover their money from earlier schemes eventually transferred their funds into the new investment.
Earlier this year, the company introduced a cryptocurrency called IBBB Coin, claiming its value would rise through the tokenisation of agarwood trees.
However, the cryptocurrency has since lost more than 99 per cent of its value, leaving buyers' holdings almost worthless, Chu said.
The company also offered an investment scheme involving automated car wash centres in mainland China, promising annual returns of 30 per cent.
During the operation, police searched the company's office and warehouse in Kwun Tong, as well as the homes of the suspects.
Police seized about HK$540,000 in cash, 25 mobile phones, computers, investment contracts and products suspected to contain agarwood.
They are examining the seized electronic devices and contacting other potential victims for further information.
On Oct 14, Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission placed the company on its alert list for suspicious investment products.

Title: Man, 67, bludgeoned to death in Permas Jaya; suspect arrested
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A 67-year-old man was found dead with head injuries after being repeatedly beaten with a blunt object in Permas Jaya, here, yesterday.
Johor Baru (Selatan) deputy police chief Superintendent Ng Swie Chait said the victim also suffered injuries to his face and arms.
He said police received a report from the public at 4.54pm before tracking down and arresting a 47-year-old man believed to have been involved in the murder.
The suspect was arrested outside an eatery in Bandar Baru Permas Jaya at 6pm.
Ng said police seized an iron walking stick and a framed portrait to assist investigations.
"Checks found that the suspect has a criminal record with two entries, including one for a drug-related offence. However, a urine test came back negative for drug abuse," he said in a statement.
The suspect has been remanded for seven days from today to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
The motive remains under investigation.
A post-mortem examination at Sultan Ismail Hospital today found that the cause of death was multiple blunt-force trauma to the head.
Police urged anyone with information on the incident to contact the district police headquarters at 07-2182323.

Title: Death in lock-up: Family lodges report against KL police chief
Article:
PETALING JAYA: The family of the late Noorizwan Zulkefly, 42, lodged a police report against Kuala Lumpur police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus here today over his remarks on the death of the detainee.
Lawyer Latheefa Koya said the report was prompted by Fadil's statements on Noorizwan's death, which she described as dishonest and an attempt to justify the incident on the grounds that the deceased had a criminal record.
"We were shocked by the statements made during yesterday's press conference because they contradicted what we had witnessed ourselves.
"This was particularly evident from our meeting with pathologist Dr Faridah on Monday, Oct 12, at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM).
"During the meeting, Dr Faridah briefed us and explained the autopsy findings, supported by photographic evidence of the injuries sustained by the deceased.
"However, the way Datuk Fadil delivered his statements at the press conference gave the impression that he was completely unaware of the pathologist's briefing and findings," she said at a press conference at the Lawyers for Liberty (LFL) office here today.
She said officers from the federal custodial death investigation unit were also present at the meeting.
Earlier, Latheefa, fellow lawyer N. Surendran, Noorizwan's brother Nooranis Zulkefly and several family members went to the Petaling Jaya district police headquarters to lodge the report at about 3pm.
In the report, Latheefa said Fadil's statements at the press conference had failed to address the severe injuries found on Noorizwan's body, as documented in the forensic findings.
"The Kuala Lumpur police chief did not mention that there were severe injuries on Noorizwan's body, despite this being a finding by the pathologist.
"He also claimed that the cause of death had yet to be finalised, although the pathologist had already informed the police and the family of the cause," she said in the report.
Latheefa said Fadil's statements were inaccurate and misleading, adding that his position as Kuala Lumpur police chief presented a conflict of interest because the case involved personnel under his command.
She said the federal police should conduct the investigation under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which deals with murder, and that the personnel involved should only be allowed to return to duty if no criminal elements were found.
Yesterday, the media reported that
police were awaiting the full report
from the Chemistry Department and the pathology findings to determine the cause of death of a man who died in custody on Oct 1.
Fadil was reported to have said that the detainee, a local man in his 40s, died at 1.52am while receiving treatment at HCTM.

Title: Teenage girl sacrifices schooling as both parents battle stage four cancer
Article:
JOHOR BARU: A teenage girl has put her education on hold to care for her parents, both battling stage four cancer.
The family is struggling to raise RM10,000 for each cycle of her mother's urgent chemotherapy.
Nur Sara Ayryna, who stopped attending school to look after her parents, now faces the heartbreaking reality of seeing both of them fight for their lives.
Her mother, Noor Diana Hashim, 47, was diagnosed with breast cancer, which has now spread to her liver, lungs, spine and neck.
Her father, — 47-year-old Iman Heart nasyid band frontman Zek Ayry Khan Zarak Khan — has nasopharyngeal cancer.
Both are unable to work and cannot afford treatment.
Noor Diana is now dependent on oxygen around the clock.
They are appealing for help because time is running out. Noor Diana needs to undergo chemotherapy as soon as possible.
She was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2021 and underwent surgery the following year.
The doctors recommended urgent chemotherapy. However, delays due to patient waiting lists had forced the family to consider private treatment, which costs about RM10,000 per cycle.
Noor Diana's left arm is swollen; it developed after her breast surgery, had worsened and further restricted her movement.
The couple's eldest son is employed, while their second son works as a motorcycle mechanic.
The couple had managed an event management company and actively volunteered to help the needy, including asnaf, single mothers, people with disabilities and flood victims, in the past.
"We were blessed with good health then and never missed opportunities to help others. Now, we are the ones being tested, and we appeal for help so my wife can receive the treatment she needs," Zek said.

Title: RM2,000 minimum wage backed by economic data, nationwide consultations
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The proposed RM2,000 minimum wage was determined through economic research and extensive consultations with employers, workers and academics, rather than an arbitrary decision, National Wages Consultative Council chairman Tan Sri Zainal Rahim Seman said.
He said the council had conducted 21 engagement sessions nationwide and commissioned a comprehensive study to ensure the proposed rate was fair to workers without placing undue pressure on employers.
The study, supported by a government allocation of between RM1 million and RM1.5 million, examined several economic indicators to determine an appropriate minimum wage.
These included the poverty line income, median wages, price indices, labour growth and gross domestic product (GDP).
"We do not use figures arbitrarily. The rate is based on studies conducted by academics and consultants, and we believe it is appropriate and reasonable.
"It should not impose an undue burden on any party," he told reporters here.
Zainal said the council had also compared Malaysia's wage levels with those of other countries before arriving at its recommendations.
Based on median wages and other economic indicators, the study produced a projected wage range of about RM1,970 to more than RM2,100.
However, he said the council had to consider the interests of both workers and employers before recommending a rate.
"We held consultations with employers, workers and trade unions. We also have five academics, including university lecturers specialising in economics, who help us with the analysis," he said.
Zainal said the wage-setting process followed a tripartite approach involving the government, employers and workers.
The objective was to strike a balance between improving employees' purchasing power and ensuring businesses could manage their operating costs.
He acknowledged that implementing a new minimum wage could present challenges, recalling similar difficulties when Malaysia introduced its first minimum wage of RM900.
"There were problems when we first introduced the minimum wage. Implementation challenges will always exist, but our responsibility is to enforce it," he said.
Under the 2027 Budget, the government announced that the national minimum wage would increase from RM1,700 to RM2,000 a month from June next year.
Micro, small and medium enterprises with annual sales below RM50 million will be exempted from the increase to allow them time to adjust.

Title: Malaysia banks on policy certainty, economic resilience to attract investment – Amir Hamzah
Article:
BANGKOK: Malaysia is strengthening its business environment, policy certainty and economic resilience to attract long-term investment, with foreign and domestic direct investments reaching record highs, said Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
He said the government was reinforcing the country's economic fundamentals through regulatory clarity, business-friendly policies and reforms to provide investors with greater certainty when operating in Malaysia.
"Malaysia recorded gross domestic product growth of more than five per cent for two consecutive years while maintaining stable inflation, despite growing geopolitical uncertainties.
"Malaysia's story is resilience," he said at the Bloomberg Global Policy Series: ASEAN Growth Markets Spotlight – Competing and Connecting for Global Capital here on Friday.
Amir Hamzah said Malaysia was also focused on moving its economy up the value chain by strengthening key industries, including semiconductors, and deepening domestic supply chains to create higher-value jobs and enhance its competitiveness in global trade.
"We want to extend the supply chain and deepen the ecosystem," he said, adding that a stronger industrial ecosystem would develop local talent, improve supply chain reliability and strengthen Malaysia's position in global trade.
Amir Hamzah said the government was also seeking to expand the role of private markets in capital formation, enabling angel investors and venture capital to support businesses and strengthen the pipeline of companies entering public markets.
He said Malaysia's domestic capital base provided a strong foundation for growth, while improved corporate governance and value creation would help enhance the attractiveness of its capital market to international investors.
He also highlighted the importance of ASEAN integration, including better-connected capital markets, more efficient cross-border payment systems and the ASEAN Power Grid, in unlocking investment opportunities and strengthening regional supply chains.
Amir Hamzah said Malaysia would continue to focus on infrastructure development, economic diversification and consistent policy implementation to support sustainable growth and ensure its benefits reached the wider population.
"Whatever clarity that we've given, we've executed along that line. No surprises," he said, stressing that policy consistency and a supportive business environment remained central to Malaysia's investment appeal.

Title: Petronas, Petrovietnam deepen energy cooperation under new pact
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) and Vietnam National Industry–Energy Group (Petrovietnam) have signed a strategic alliance agreement to strengthen cooperation across the energy value chain.
The agreement, which marks 35 years of collaboration between the two companies, will see them explore opportunities in upstream development, gas and liquefied natural gas, downstream activities and low-carbon solutions.
It was signed at Petrovietnam's headquarters by Petronas president and group chief executive officer Tan Sri Tengku Muhammad Taufik and Petrovietnam president and chief executive officer Le Manh Cuong.
The two companies subsequently exchanged documents at Vietnam's government headquarters in a ceremony witnessed by Prime Minister Le Minh Hung.
The exchange involved Tengku Muhammad Taufik and Petrovietnam chairman Le Ngoc Son.
In a statement, Petronas said it remained committed to supporting Vietnam's evolving energy needs while exploring broader opportunities for regional energy cooperation.
The national oil company entered Vietnam in 1991 as one of the country's pioneering foreign investors in the upstream oil and gas sector.
It has since expanded its presence into petrochemicals, renewable energy and LNG through partnerships with Petrovietnam and other Vietnamese companies.
Their cooperation also extends to regional initiatives, including a tripartite renewable energy project involving Malaysia, Vietnam and Singapore.

Title: Subang-Laos drug jet: Cops await Philippine confirmation on politician's role
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Police are awaiting confirmation from the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency (PDEA) on claims that a Filipino politician funded the charter of a private jet used to transport 521kg of syabu from Subang to Laos.
Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said police had identified two Filipinos who booked the private jet.
"The Philippine syndicate hired private aviation services to transport drugs from Laos to the Philippines.
"We are still awaiting official confirmation from the Philippine authorities on whether a politician there was involved in the syndicate.
"That is what we have gathered so far based on media reports from the country," he told a press conference at the Johor police contingent headquarters.
Yesterday, Manila media reported PDEA spokesman Joseph Frederick Calulut as saying that a politician from Mindanao in the southern Philippines had
allegedly funded the rental of a private jet
carrying 521kg of syabu worth 3.54 billion pesos in Laos.
Reports also said the politician had paid about 3.1 million pesos (RM200,880) to charter the aircraft.

Title: Two TNB contractors critically injured by electric shock as substation fire triggers Johor Bahru blackout (VIDEO)
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 16 — Two Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB) contractors were critically injured after suffering electric shocks during maintenance work at the utility company’s Kangkar Tebrau main intake substation here this evening.
The incident triggered a fire and disrupted electricity supply in parts of Johor Bahru.
TNB said the fire broke out at 6.03pm, interrupting power supply in several areas around Johor Jaya and its surrounding areas.
“TNB’s technical team has been deployed to the site and is actively working to restore electricity supply to the affected consumers,” the electricity company said in a statement.
The national electricity company also apologised for the inconvenience caused.
The Johor Fire and Rescue Department said the Tebrau fire station received a distress call about the incident at 6.10pm.
