Title: Zahid says Malaysia ready to help Indonesia fight forest fires after Prabowo accepts foreign aid
Article:
TIANJIN, Oct 16 — Malaysia is ready to help Indonesia tackle widespread forest and land fires after President Prabowo Subianto agreed to accept offers of assistance from neighbouring countries.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Malaysia welcomed the Indonesian government’s openness to receiving foreign assistance to fight the fires.
He said that although Malaysia’s offer might be modest, Putrajaya remained committed to helping its neighbour in the spirit of friendship and strong bilateral ties.
“We are grateful to the Indonesian government and President Prabowo for being open to accepting foreign assistance to tackle the forest fires.
“Even though the help we have offered is small, Malaysia is prepared to send aid to assist our neighbour,” he said, adding that Malaysia valued Prabowo’s openness on the matter.
He made the remarks to Malaysian journalists during an afternoon tea session shortly before departing China today, following a five-day working visit.
Buildings are shrouded in haze from Indonesian fires in Kuala Lumpur on October 16, 2026. — AFP pic
Earlier, Indonesian Foreign Ministry official Arrmanatha Nasir reportedly said President Prabowo had approved offers of assistance from neighbouring countries, with technical discussions underway to determine how the aid would be delivered.
However, Arrmanatha did not specify which countries had offered assistance or what form it would take.
Malaysia had previously offered to deploy a Bombardier CL-415MP aircraft, three helicopters and 52 personnel to help Indonesia tackle the fires.
On September 19, Ahmad Zahid said Prabowo had accepted the offer during a meeting the previous day in Hambalang, West Java. — Bernama

Title: Perlis MACC recovers nearly RM700,000 through forfeitures since 2024
Article:
ARAU, Oct 16 — The Perlis Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has recovered RM698,255.55 through forfeitures from 2024 to date.
Perlis MACC director Mohd Nor Adha Ab Gani said the state anti-graft agency opened 65 investigation papers (IPs), recorded 84 arrests and brought 37 charges to court during the period.
“According to the annual breakdown, 20 IPs were opened in 2024 involving 27 arrests and 13 charges, with a forfeiture value of RM323,872.55. In 2025, 22 investigation papers were opened, 34 arrests were recorded, and 16 charges were brought to court, with a forfeiture value of RM374,168.
“As for 2026, Perlis MACC opened 23 investigation papers, recorded 23 arrests, and brought eight charges to court, with a forfeiture value of RM215,” he was quoted as saying in a statement issued by Istana Arau today.
The statement said the outgoing director presented the figures to the Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail during a recent farewell ceremony at Istana Arau.
Mohd Nor Adha said Perlis MACC also focused on preventive measures, submitting 61 Governance Improvement Recommendations to federal and state departments and statutory bodies.
“These efforts aim to strengthen the public service delivery system, enhance organisational integrity, and close gaps and opportunities for corruption to occur,” he said.
He said Perlis MACC personnel had also received several accolades in recognition of their commitment and performance, including the Chief Commissioner Special Award for 2024 and 2025.
“Perlis MACC also won the Best KPI Management Award 2025 with an evaluation score of 97.45 per cent, besides securing third place for the Best Financial Management Award 2025.
“These achievements demonstrate the dedication of Perlis MACC in balancing enforcement action with continuous preventive measures to foster an administrative environment of integrity, transparency, and accountability,” he said.
At the farewell ceremony, Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra thanked Mohd Nor Adha for his service and commitment in leading Perlis MACC for two years and seven months, from March 1, 2024, until tomorrow.
His Royal Highness also congratulated him on his promotion and appointment as Terengganu MACC director, effective October 18.
The Raja Muda expressed hope that the experience Mohd Nor Adha gained in Perlis would help him in his new role and in continuing efforts to strengthen integrity, governance and anti-corruption initiatives. — Bernama

Title: El Niño could hit fishermen, fish farms as temperatures soar to 40°C, says Mat Sabu
Article:
KOTA BHARU, Oct 16 — Coastal fishermen and aquaculture operators could be hit if El Niño pushes temperatures up to 40°Celsius, prompting calls for early preparations to protect the country’s food production.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the phenomenon could drive fish farther out to sea, posing a challenge for coastal fishermen who lack the capacity to fish in deeper waters.
He said the government had discussed preparations for El Niño with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim as part of efforts to strengthen national food security.
“Among the measures is an increase in allocations for coastal fishermen; during an El Niño event, temperatures can climb as high as 40 degrees Celsius, which significantly impacts them.
“Fish tend to migrate further offshore, yet coastal fishermen are generally restricted to fishing within a five-nautical-mile radius; they are not equipped to venture further out or fish in deeper waters,” he told reporters after attending the 2026 Kelantan State-level Convention of Parti Amanah Negara here today.
Mohamad said the aquaculture sector could also face challenges if temperatures rise significantly, particularly over the cost of installing protective measures such as canvas covers over fish-rearing ponds.
He said early preparations were crucial to help farmers and other agrifood operators mitigate the effects of hot weather on their activities.
Timely dissemination of information to these groups was also essential to help them take appropriate measures, he added.
Mohamad said the possibility of haze further complicated preparations for the potential impacts of El Niño. — Bernama

Title: ‘They were aware’: Bukit Aman on five Malaysians held in Tokyo with cocaine in their shoes
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 16 — Five Malaysians arrested for concealing five kilograms of cocaine in their shoe soles at Haneda International Airport in Tokyo, Japan, on October 10 are believed to have been drug mules paid RM8,000 each.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the suspects, aged between 19 and 26, were each given the shoes by a drug syndicate that is still being identified.
“We believe they (the suspects) were aware of what they were carrying, which is an illegal substance,” he told a press conference at the Johor Contingent Police Headquarters here today.
He said police were investigating whether all the suspects were directly involved in the syndicate and whether they had previously travelled to other countries using the same modus operandi.
He added that initial checks showed none of the five suspects had a criminal record.
Hussein said all the suspects, including a married couple, were believed to have travelled to Japan for a holiday before being detained by the authorities.
“The group was led by the woman’s husband, and she invited her friends for a trip to Japan, with each given a pair of shoes that had been pre-stuffed with drugs,” he said.
He said another Malaysian, who was not arrested in connection with the case, was a travel agent and had been cleared of involvement.
Hussein previously said checks confirmed that the group had departed from Terminal 2 of Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA).
Japanese customs authorities found the drugs inside the shoe soles worn by all the suspects.
He said the NCID had sent a team to Japan to investigate and gather details of the case.
On the drug seizure in Laos, he confirmed that the illicit substances transported on a private jet had been ordered by two Filipino nationals.
He said police were working with the Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency to track down the individuals and the syndicate involved.
He also said the Royal Malaysia Police were awaiting confirmation on whether the syndicate involved politicians in the Philippines, as reported by the media there.
On October 1, Laotian police seized 521 kilograms of crystal methamphetamine inside a Learjet private aircraft that had arrived from Subang at Luang Prabang International Airport in Laos.
Following the incident, 13 individuals, including Malaysian, Singaporean and Philippine nationals, were detained by Laotian authorities to assist investigations into the transnational drug trafficking case.
On October 7, police arrested a local man, the owner of the private jet, during a raid at Sultan Abdul Aziz Shah Airport. — Bernama

Title: Wet and windy: MetMalaysia warns of thunderstorms in 11 states and Putrajaya until 8pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are forecast across Perlis, Melaka, Putrajaya and parts of nine other states until 8 pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
In Kedah, the affected areas include Kubang Pasu, Sik, Baling, Kuala Muda, Langkawi and Padang Terap, while in Perak, the weather alert covers Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Larut, Matang and Selama, Kerian, Kinta, Perak Tengah, Manjung, Hilir Perak and Bagan Datuk.
In Kelantan, the warning covers Gua Musang, Kuala Krai, Jeli, Tanah Merah and Machang, while in Terengganu, it affects Kemaman, Dungun and Hulu Terengganu.
In Pahang, the areas involved are Jerantut and Kuantan, while in Selangor, they comprise Petaling, Klang, Kuala Selangor, Kuala Langat, Sepang, Sabak Bernam and Hulu Langat, alongside Tampin in Negeri Sembilan.
In Sarawak, the alert covers Kuching, Samarahan, Serian, Sri Aman, Betong, Mukah, Sarikei, Sibu, Kapit (Song), Bintulu, Limbang and Miri (Marudi, Bario and Telang Usan).
In Sabah, the warning involves the Interior (Sipitang, Tenom, Pensiangan, Membakut, Beaufort, Tambunan, Keningau and Sook), West Coast (Kota Belud, Tuaran, Kota Kinabalu, Papar, Penampang and Ranau), Sandakan (Kinabatangan and Tongod) and Kudat (Kota Marudu). — Bernama

Title: AAIB flags firefighting gaps at Sarawak airstrip after crash killed five
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Air Accidents Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has urged the operator of Long Lellang Short Take-Off and Landing Port (STOLport) in Miri, Sarawak, to review its rescue and firefighting arrangements after a helicopter crash killed five people, including four Health Ministry personnel, on September 8.
The AAIB recommended that aerodrome operator Malaysia Airports Sdn Bhd (MASB) review rescue and firefighting arrangements across its STOLports to ensure auxiliary personnel were properly trained and equipped, and that firefighting equipment and personal protective equipment (PPE) were properly maintained and serviceable.
The bureau said the recommendation followed findings that Malaysia Volunteers Corps Department (Rela) personnel assigned to auxiliary rescue and firefighting duties had responded to the blaze without appropriate firefighting PPE.
“Some of the available PPE exhibited visible signs of deterioration and damage, which could adversely affect the safety and effectiveness of the emergency response,” the AAIB said in its preliminary report.
The report said 12 dry powder fire extinguishers at the STOLport terminal were used by responders and local villagers in an attempt to put out the flames, but the fire continued to burn for several hours.
All five occupants on board – a 30-year-old Malaysian pilot and four Health Ministry personnel – died from severe burn injuries, according to post-mortem findings cited in the report.
The Messerschmitt-Bölkow-Blohm BO105 S helicopter, registered as 9M-LLF and operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd under the callsign MEDIC3, was conducting a scheduled Flying Doctor Service flight.
The aircraft is designed for various operations, including passenger transport, utility work, medical evacuation and other specialised missions, with a maximum take-off mass of about 2,500kg, depending on its configuration.
The report said a 37-second ground-based video captured the helicopter’s final moments, showing it in flight with a visible smoke trail and apparent flames behind the main gearbox as it approached Runway 04.
The helicopter came to rest about 25 metres from the runway threshold and was destroyed by fire.
All communication frequencies were operating normally, and no emergency call or distress transmission from the helicopter was recorded between departure and the crash, the report said.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department found that weather conditions near Long Lellang STOLport were generally good, with horizontal visibility exceeding 10km during the period assessed.
As an immediate safety measure, Layang-Layang Aerospace suspended operations of aircraft fitted with the same engine type pending airworthiness verification.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia cleared the affected aircraft to return to service on September 13 after technical reviews, the report said.
A detailed examination of the wreckage will be conducted to establish the nature and extent of the damage and, where possible, the sequence and development of the fire and ground-contact damage. The findings will be included in the final report.
The Transport Ministry said information in the preliminary report could be revised as additional evidence emerged, while a comprehensive analysis and the investigation’s conclusions would be presented in the final report.
The ministry said the investigation was intended to prevent similar accidents from recurring, rather than determine fault or liability.
“The ministry appreciates the efforts of the AAIB and the cooperation of all parties involved in assisting the investigation, and remains committed to strengthening the country’s aviation safety,” it said. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: Rela stands for Jabatan Sukarelawan Malaysia, or the Malaysia Volunteers Corps Department in English.

Title: Haze watch: 29 areas recording unhealthy or worse air, Larkin, Pasir Gudang API hits 202
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Air quality in Larkin and Pasir Gudang, Johor, deteriorated to very unhealthy levels this evening, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) reaching 202 as at 5.30pm, while 27 other areas nationwide recorded unhealthy readings.
According to the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, six other areas in Johor recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Pengerang (181), Batu Pahat and Kota Tinggi (171 each), Kluang (168), Tangkak (159) and Segamat (156).
In Selangor, Johan Setia recorded the highest reading at 184, followed by Klang (176), Petaling Jaya (173), Shah Alam (168), Banting (162) and Kuala Selangor (152).
Three stations in Negeri Sembilan also recorded unhealthy readings: Nilai (181), Seremban (174) and Port Dickson (170).
In Melaka, Bandaraya Melaka recorded an API of 180, followed by Bukit Rambai (175) and Alor Gajah (169).
In Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda and Cheras both recorded an API of 163, while Putrajaya registered 170.
Unhealthy air quality was also reported in Perak at Seri Manjung (160) and Tanjung Malim (158); in Pahang at Temerloh (139) and Rompin (103); and in Sabah at Tawau (153) and Sandakan (107).
Across the country, 27 areas recorded moderate API readings, while Sarikei in Sarawak was the only station with good air quality, at 50.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy; and above 300, hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Fatal Senawang crash: Lorry rammed into JPJ car during roadside inspection, police say
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 16 — A lorry carrying dry food products lost control and crashed into a Road Transport Department (JPJ) car and another lorry during a roadside inspection, killing a JPJ officer and injuring three others on the North-South Expressway near Senawang, police said today.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the two JPJ personnel had been inspecting a motoloader carrying a cabin load on the emergency lane at Kilometre 256.1 northbound when the lorry approached from behind at about 10.30pm yesterday.
“However, the lorry lost control and failed to avoid the vehicles, crashing into the rear of the JPJ car and the motoloader,” he said in a statement.
The 42-year-old JPJ officer suffered head injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.
His 32-year-old colleague sustained serious head injuries and injuries to several parts of his body and was receiving treatment at Tuanku Ja’afar Seremban Hospital.
The two lorry drivers, aged 44 and 48, also suffered injuries to their legs and bodies and were receiving treatment at the hospital’s emergency department.
Alzafny said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He urged anyone with information about the crash to contact investigating officer Inspector Syakinah Ahmad at 06-6033394 or visit the nearest police station to assist with investigations.
* Editor’s note: JPJ stands for Jabatan Pengangkutan Jalan in Malay, or the Road Transport Department in English. PLUS is the Malay abbreviation for Projek Lebuhraya Utara-Selatan, the operator of the North-South Expressway.

Title: Transport minister vows action if negligence found in Senawang fatal crash involving JPJ officers
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The Road Transport Department (JPJ) will provide full cooperation to the Royal Malaysia Police to ensure that investigations into the accident that claimed the life of one of its personnel at KM256 of the North-South Expressway, near the Senawang exit last night, are conducted thoroughly and transparently.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke said appropriate action would be taken against any party found to have violated the law or committed misconduct or negligence, based on the investigation findings.
“If there are any legal violations, misconduct or negligence identified through the investigation, appropriate action will be taken against the responsible parties in accordance with the provisions of the law and regulations in force,” he said in a statement today.
Loke expressed deep sorrow and extended his condolences to the family of Negeri Sembilan JPJ Enforcement Assistant Grade KP2 Mohd Azrul Rashid Yaakub, who was killed in the accident while on duty.
“The passing of Mohd Azrul is a great loss, particularly to his family and colleagues who have served alongside him. His sacrifice and dedication in carrying out his duties for the safety of road users will always be appreciated,” he said.
Loke also prayed for a speedy recovery for Motor Vehicle Examiner Grade AB2 Nor Amirudin Rameli, who suffered serious injuries in the incident, and for ease in all matters throughout his medical treatment.
He added that JPJ director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli visited the families of both officers this morning to convey his condolences and offer support.
Loke said the Transport Ministry and JPJ would continue to look into the welfare and needs of the deceased officer’s family and the injured officer, including ensuring that appropriate assistance was channelled to them.
Earlier, media reports said one JPJ personnel had died while another was seriously injured in an accident involving the department’s vehicle and two lorries on the southbound North-South Expressway near the Senawang exit last night.
The incident occurred at about 10.50pm while JPJ personnel were inspecting a lorry in the emergency lane.
Another lorry approaching from behind allegedly lost control before crashing into the JPJ sport utility vehicle (SUV) and the lorry being inspected. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: JPJ stands for Jabatan Pengangkutan Jalan, or the Road Transport Department in English.

Title: Want OKU status? Here’s how the Welfare Dept evaluates applications
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The registration of persons with disabilities (OKU) follows the OKU Registration Guidelines (2019 Amendment), jointly developed by the Social Welfare Department (JKM) and the Health Ministry.
In a statement today, JKM said the process also involves medical specialists who sit on the OKU Registration Committee under the National Council for Persons with Disabilities.
The department said the guidelines ensure the evaluation and registration process is conducted professionally, systematically and based on established criteria.
Medical officers, practitioners or specialists assess an individual’s functionality and disability using the OKU Registration Application Form (BPPOKU Amendment 2/2019), it said.
JKM added that the assessment measures an individual’s level of functioning across seven domains, including self-care, mobility and dexterity.
The OKU Registrar will not approve applications that fail to meet the criteria in the relevant domains.
“However, applicants have the right to appeal the decision under Section 24 (2) of the Persons with Disabilities Act 2008,” JKM said.
The department stressed that individuals requiring welfare support will receive due consideration based on their needs and existing policies.
It remains committed to ensuring the well-being of vulnerable groups through appropriate aid and services tailored to individual needs. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: OKU stands for Orang Kurang Upaya, the Malay term for persons with disabilities. JKM stands for Jabatan Kebajikan Masyarakat, or the Social Welfare Department in English.

Title: Govt overpaid Semantan Estate up to RM500,000 for Duta Enclave land, property valuer tells court
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The High Court was told today that the Malaysian Government had overpaid Semantan Estate Sdn Bhd (1952) between RM400,000 and RM500,000 in compensation for the acquisition of 263.272 acres of land known as the Duta Enclave in 1956.
Finance Ministry Valuation and Property Services Department (JPPH) assistant director Tan Tat Khuan said his assessment valued the land in Mukim Batu at RM875,000, compared with the RM1.39 million paid by the government.
“Deducting my valuation of RM875,000 from the RM1.39 million already paid shows that the government overpaid by between RM400,000 and RM500,000.
“If the court accepts my valuation, no additional compensation should be paid to the plaintiff (Semantan Estate),” he said.
Tan, the government’s sole witness, was testifying during the compensation assessment hearing before Judge Roslan Mat Nor.
Under further questioning by senior federal counsel Nurhafizza Azizan, Tan confirmed that his assessment showed the government had overpaid.
In earlier proceedings, Tan testified that the government paid Semantan Estate RM1.39 million in compensation in 1965, exceeding his recommended amount.
He said he had also assessed the land using a different acreage and arrived at a compensation value of RM985,000.
Asked by Judge Roslan whether additional compensation would be payable based on that valuation, Tan said none would be due. However, he clarified that his recommended compensation amounts excluded interest.
During questioning by Semantan Estate’s lawyer Ira Biswas, Tan rejected suggestions that information obtained from valuers A.A. Wragg and A.I.G. Harding, who assessed the land in 1956 and 1958 respectively, amounted to hearsay because they had not testified in court.
“In my view, both reports are consistent and reliable,” he said.
The hearing resumes on Nov 23.
On Nov 13, 2025, the Federal Court dismissed Semantan Estate’s application for leave to appeal against a Court of Appeal ruling that the Federal Territory Registrar of Titles was not required to register the 263.272-acre Duta Enclave land in the company’s name.
The decision upheld the government’s position, and the case was returned to the High Court for an assessment of compensation.
On June 24, 2025, the Court of Appeal ruled that Semantan Estate was not entitled to ownership of the land but was entitled to appropriate compensation based on its value in 1956, when it was acquired by the government.
The prime Jalan Duta site houses several landmarks, including the Inland Revenue Board complex, government buildings, the National Hockey Stadium, the Institute of Islamic Understanding Malaysia and the Federal Territory Mosque.
Semantan Estate sued the government for trespass in 2003, alleging that the land had been unlawfully acquired.
In 2009, Judicial Commissioner Zura Yahya ruled that Semantan Estate retained beneficial interest in the 263.27-acre site, which the government had unlawfully acquired and occupied. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: The initials JPPH in Malay stands for Jabatan Penilaian dan Perkhidmatan Harta, or the Valuation and Property Services Department in English.

Title: PeKa B40 becomes PeKa Sihat in healthcare revamp as govt looks to ease clinic queues
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Health Ministry’s PeKa B40 healthcare programme will be rebranded as PeKa Sihat, with changes aimed at making the initiative more effective and easing congestion at public health clinics, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
He said the Cabinet had agreed to the proposed amendments to the programme, which focuses on addressing non-communicable diseases.
“The Cabinet has agreed to the proposed amendments to the PeKa B40 programme under the Health Ministry, taking into account of its effectiveness in tackling non-communicable diseases.
“The Health Ministry is coordinating several measures to make the programme more effective — including alleviating congestion at public health clinics by utilising participating clinics in the PeKa B40 initiative,” he said at the weekly post-Cabinet media briefing, which was broadcast live today.
Fahmi said the Health Ministry would announce further details of the rebranded PeKa Sihat programme.
PeKa B40 – or known in Malay as Skim Peduli Kesihatan untuk Kumpulan B40 – was launched in 2019 to support the healthcare needs of lower-income groups, with a focus on the early detection and management of non-communicable diseases.
The programme is administered by ProtectHealth Corporation Sdn Bhd, a wholly owned subsidiary of ProtectHealth Malaysia, which operates under the Health Ministry.

Title: Splitting the AG’s two hats: Azalina takes charge of talks with select committee
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Law and Institutional Reform Minister Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said has been tasked with engaging a Parliamentary Special Select Committee on constitutional amendments to separate the roles of the Attorney General and the Public Prosecutor.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim made the announcement after a decree by the Malay Rulers on the proposed amendments at the recent Conference of Rulers meeting, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
“The prime minister has instructed Datuk Seri Azalina to conduct the engagements and discussions with the Parliamentary Special Select Committee, which has already prepared a draft for the constitutional amendments,” Fahmi said at the weekly post-Cabinet media briefing, which was broadcast live.
“Any amendments or recommendations will then be communicated back to the Conference of Rulers,” he said.
Fahmi said the Cabinet was also briefed on the outcome of Anwar’s audience with the Conference of Rulers on proposed amendments to the prime minister’s tenure.
He said both proposals are part of the government’s key institutional reform efforts and need further refinement before they can proceed.
Separately, Fahmi said the Cabinet was told that Parliament now falls entirely under the Parliamentary Service Council, effectively ending executive control over its administration.
“This fulfills one of our promises and represents a significant institutional reform effort,” he said.

Title: Fahmi: No Malaysian palm oil companies involved in burning activities in Indonesia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — There are no Malaysian plantation companies with palm oil concessions in Indonesia that were involved in forest fires linked to the regional haze issue, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil.
He said this was based on cross-reference checks conducted with local companies that maintain palm oil concessions in Indonesia.
“Plantation and Commodities Minister Datuk Seri Noraini Ahmad informed the Cabinet that the burning activities occurred outside of the concession areas owned by Malaysian companies,” he said at the weekly post-Cabinet media briefing, which was broadcast live today.
Fahmi, who is also the unity government spokesman, added that one Malaysian-owned plantation under Genting Plantations saw a fire from outside spread into its land.
He said the fire, which affected five hectares of land, has since been put out.
“The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) will continue to have engagement sessions with Malaysian plantation companies that have their operations in Indonesia,” he said.
Fahmi added that Malaysia would review the assistance it had earlier offered to Indonesia to fight the forest fires, such as the deployment of assets, as the situation had changed.
He explained that this was to ensure the assistance given by Malaysia would be effective.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said the Health, Education, and Youth and Sports ministries had informed the Cabinet of the need for closer coordination to tackle the haze issue, including steps on outdoor activities and learning centres.
He added that the Education and Health ministries said their current guidelines followed the National Haze Action Plan.
“The Prime Minister’s Office will chair a meeting this Monday (Oct 19), and the haze will be one of the issues on the agenda.
“We expect more information after the meeting, including updates from the various ministries,” he said.

Title: Pakatan confident of Melaka win, but Amirudin says voters will decide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is confident of winning the upcoming Melaka state election, while acknowledging that the outcome ultimately rests with voters.
The coalition’s election director, Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari, said PH would announce its candidates for the state election on Oct 24, after he finalises the list with the coalition’s president and top party leaders.
“I am confident we will win, God willing. Politicians will always be asked whether they are confident of winning. But the outcome is determined by the voters,” he told reporters when asked about PH’s prospects in the Melaka polls.
Amirudin, who is also the Selangor menteri besar, said the candidates had been identified about two years ago, adding that the line-up would comprise individuals of different ages and backgrounds, including professionals and those with political experience.
He did not disclose the names of the candidates.
Yesterday, PH communications director Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said discussions on candidates for the Melaka state election were over 95 per cent complete.
Fahmi, who is also communications minister, said PH had scheduled its candidate announcement for Oct 24, with the venue to be confirmed later.
The candidate announcement and launch of the PH election machinery for the 16th Melaka state election, originally scheduled for this Sunday, had been postponed.
The Election Commission (EC) has set Oct 31 for nominations, Nov 10 for early voting and Nov 14 for polling, following the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly on Sept 23.
In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.

Title: Italian cyclist targeted by stone-throwing teens while camping in Sabah
Article:
RANAU, Oct 16 — Police have launched an investigation into a viral video showing a group of teenagers allegedly throwing stones at an Italian cyclist who was camping at Kampung Lohan while on a solo cycling expedition around Sabah.
Ranau District Police Chief Supt Mursalin Mahmud said a special team had been formed to investigate the incident after the video attracted public attention.
The cyclist, Nicola Chiacchio, had stopped at the Kampung Lohan field during his journey around Sabah using a bicycle.
While resting at the field, he was approached by local residents who offered him food and water, while children also took the opportunity to meet and greet the traveller.
However, while he was preparing to sleep on the night of Oct 8, a group of teenagers allegedly threw stones towards him, apparently in an attempt to frighten him.
Chiacchio subsequently uploaded a video of the incident on social media, prompting concern among members of the Ranau community and criticism of the teenagers’ actions.
The video was later removed on Oct 9 after the Italian traveller said he did not want the matter to become more serious.
He reportedly said his intention in uploading the video initially was to raise awareness and remind those involved, particularly parents, about the consequences of such behaviour.
Police investigations included interviewing the traveller, visiting the location where the incident occurred and speaking to several individuals connected to the incident.
Senior police officers also met the person who had allowed Chiacchio to put up his tent at the Kampung Lohan field.
Police later managed to trace Chiacchio to Cinta Mata Camp in Pitas, where officers and personnel were deployed to conduct further investigations.
Mursalin said Chiacchio had travelled through several districts during his solo cycling expedition, with Ranau being one of his stops before he continued towards Kota Marudu and subsequently Pitas.
The traveller did not lodge a police report over the incident, as he believed the teenagers had merely intended to scare him and had no intention of causing injury.
He also indicated that some of the youths had reportedly apologised to him through social media.
Mursalin nevertheless stressed that police viewed the incident seriously and advised members of the public, particularly young people, to think carefully about the consequences of their actions.
He thanked Ranau residents for their concern and continued cooperation in providing information to police to safeguard peace and security in the district.
He also praised the local community for its hospitality and for generally showing care and appreciation towards visitors and tourists who stop in Ranau.
The incident has  highlighted the importance of maintaining Sabah’s reputation for hospitality and tolerance, particularly as the State welcomes visitors from different countries.
Chiacchio’s journey has taken him through various parts of Sabah, with his decision to travel around the State entirely by bicycle attracting interest from local communities along the way. — Daily Express

Title: Human Resources Ministry to introduce Starting Basic Salary Guidelines in June 2027 rollout
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 16 — The Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma) is preparing special guidelines to ensure the orderly implementation of the Minimum Wage Order, including for semi-skilled workers and graduates, as announced in Budget 2027.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the Starting Basic Salary Guidelines based on the Malaysian Standard Classification of Occupations (Masco) would provide more comprehensive starting basic salary benchmarks according to job types and qualification levels.
“The salary guidelines for Masco categories 1 to 3 have been determined based on the findings of the Graduate Study, following several engagement sessions.
“The guidelines have also taken into account the starting basic salary recommendations under the Progressive Wage Policy (DGP), complementing the salary guidelines for Masco categories 4 to 8,” he told a press conference on the 2027 Minimum Wage Order here today.
For graduate-level jobs, Ramanan said Kesuma had proposed salary benchmarks for Masco categories 1 to 3, covering graduates with degrees, diplomas and Malaysian Advanced Skills Diplomas at Level 5.
The proposal also covers holders of Malaysian Skills Diplomas at Level 4 and Malaysian Skills Certificates at Level 3, which will initially be implemented in the form of guidelines.
“For semi-skilled jobs, Kesuma will align this approach with the Skills-Based Starting Basic Salary Guidelines.
“This includes holders of Malaysian Skills Certificates at Levels 1 and 2, enabling the starting basic salary framework to be expanded more comprehensively across Masco categories 1 to 8,” he said.
Ramanan said Kesuma was also refining a mechanism to monitor workers’ salary payments through the e-wages module, which would facilitate and strengthen the enforcement of labour laws.
The initiative is intended, among other things, to ensure that salaries are paid through methods stipulated under the Employment Act 1955 and reduce cases of unpaid or delayed wages, incorrect salary payments and wages below the minimum wage rate.
“The e-wages mechanism will be proposed for application to all workers, including non-citizens,” he said.
At the same time, Ramanan said Kesuma would take the necessary steps to amend the National Wages Consultative Council Act 2011 [Act 732] to incorporate educational qualification requirements.
This would enable minimum wage payments for graduates to be made mandatory in the future, as the Act currently contains no specific provision for setting minimum wages based on educational qualifications.
“Kesuma aims to publish and implement these guidelines alongside the implementation of the Minimum Wage Order in June 2027.
“This approach will provide employers and workers with a clearer, centralised reference for starting basic salaries according to occupation, qualifications and skills,” he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had earlier said the government had agreed to raise the minimum wage from RM1,700 to RM2,000, effective June 2027, benefiting more than four million workers.
Anwar was reported to have said that micro, small and medium enterprises with annual sales below RM50 million would be exempted from implementing the new rate to allow them time to adjust their business models.
He said the government would also introduce reforms to the workers’ income framework, including an initial minimum monthly wage of RM2,500 for semi-skilled jobs and graduates. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia unveils six homegrown chips worth RM300m as it shifts from making to designing semiconductors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Malaysia today unveiled six homegrown semiconductor innovations with an estimated combined sales potential of RM300 million, as the government seeks to move the country beyond chip manufacturing into designing and owning its own technology.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Nasir said the six innovations demonstrated the growing capabilities of Malaysian companies, although further work was needed to secure customers, meet industry qualification requirements and turn the designs into commercially successful products.
“The next milestone is to secure customer adoption, meet industry qualification requirements and scale these innovations into successful commercial products,” he said in his speech at the launch of the six chips at the Grand Hyatt here.
The innovations were developed by companies operating within the Malaysia Semiconductor IC Design Park, with applications ranging from artificial intelligence (AI) and automotive electronics to satellites and autonomous drones.
SkyeChip’s MARS1000 is an edge-AI processor intended for use in cameras, robots and factory systems, while MaiStorage’s aiDAPTIV+ provides storage solutions for AI personal computers and servers.
SiliconX unveiled what was described as Malaysia’s and Southeast Asia’s first homegrown field-programmable gate array (FPGA), a reprogrammable semiconductor device designed for industrial and automotive applications.
The other innovations are Infinecs’ Maxwell, an automotive-grade power regulator for vehicle electronics; Weeroc Space’s power controller chip for satellites and other space systems; and Alphaswift’s FC Mini flight controller for autonomous drones.
Akmal said Malaysia was building on its established strengths in semiconductor packaging, testing and related manufacturing activities, while expanding into integrated circuit (IC) design through partnerships, talent development and investment.
“Over the past decade, we have proven our expertise in testing, documentation and packaging. At the same time, looking at those strengths, Malaysia has embarked on collaboration with Arm Limited, for example, to gain access to IP design,” he told reporters after the event.
He said the government was also investing in talent development and working with industry partners to complete the semiconductor ecosystem, adding that turning the six designs into viable products would be a long journey.
Malaysia’s National Semiconductor Strategy aims to train and upskill 60,000 engineers, while the Arm On-Demand Training programme targets 10,000 Malaysian talents in specialised IC design skills over four years.
Akmal said the government also needed to develop markets for locally designed chips so that Malaysian products could attract more customers and encourage further investment in the industry.
“The effort is not just to create, but also to continue to build up markets so that what we produce will continue to open up space for additional companies to be interested in our chips,” he said.
Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the two Malaysia Semiconductor IC Design Parks in Puchong and Cyberjaya housed 407 engineers across 20 companies, including Malaysian firms and international partners from Taiwan, France, Japan and Australia.
The Puchong park, which opened in August 2024, was almost full, while the Cyberjaya facility, launched in November 2025, was preparing to expand from one occupied floor to three, he said.
Amirudin said the development of local chip-design capabilities depended on bringing together talent, technology and capital.
He cited the Advanced Semiconductor Academy of Malaysia, which has trained around 850 engineers in collaboration with more than 100 universities, and the Ehsan Semiconductor Fund, which aims to raise RM100 million to invest in early-stage semiconductor start-ups and AI application companies.
Akmal also said federal and state governments needed to coordinate their efforts to strengthen Malaysia’s overall semiconductor ecosystem, rather than view investments in different states as competing initiatives.
Responding to a question about Sarawak’s recent unveiling of a locally designed gallium nitride chip, he said each state could contribute different strengths and expertise to the industry.
“For us as a small country, definitely we need to rely on each other’s strengths,” he said, adding that investments in individual states could create value nationally if supported by better coordination.
“We need to further coordinate so that everyone will actually amplify our strength as a nation.”

Title: Children’s Court closes case of five teenage girls accused of verbally abusing Zara Qairina, submissions set for Nov 16
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 16 — The case involving five teenage girls charged with allegedly uttering abusive words against Zara Qairina Mahathir at the Children’s Court has closed, with submissions scheduled for November 16.
Counsel Joan Goh, who represents one of the teenagers, said the court had fixed November 30 for the reply submissions, followed by clarification on December 4 before a date would be set for the ruling on whether a prima facie case had been established.
She said more than 20 witnesses had testified during the hearing, but not all child witnesses testified in the Children’s Court and Zara’s mother had also not taken the stand.
The five girls are jointly charged under Section 507C(1), read with Section 34 of the Penal Code, with allegedly using abusive or insulting words against Zara, which were heard by the victim and could have caused her distress, between 10pm and 11pm on July 15.
The offence carries a jail term of up to one year, a fine, or both upon conviction, while Goh, Datuk Ram Singh and Elmer Prem Gunasan represented one of the teenagers, with the other four represented by Azhier Farhan Arisin, Abdul Fikry Jaafar, Fareez Salleh and Sylyester Kuan, all acting pro bono. — Daily Express

Title: ‘Until he retracts, go away’: Tuanku Muhriz rebukes Negeri Sembilan MB in public
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, publicly reprimanded Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim as the state’s constitutional crisis drags on.
Videos circulating on social media show the ruler telling a group of people that Ismail had written to the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal to say that Tuanku Muhriz was no longer the state’s Yang Dipertuan Besar.
A visibly angry Tuanku Muhriz then asked why the menteri besar wanted an audience with him.
“Why does he want to see me? Until he retracts what he said earlier, go away,” he said, before turning to address Ismail directly.
“Don’t see me, I don’t want to see you. You understand? I am the Yang Dipertuan Besar but you said I am not.”
Ismail responded with the angkat sembah, the customary gesture of greeting royalty.
Worshippers at the mosque were heard chanting “Daulat Tuanku” after the reprimand.
Negeri Sembilan has been gripped by a royal crisis since April, when four individuals claiming to be undang, or chieftains, declared that Tuanku Muhriz had been removed as ruler.
In June, the same disputed undang purportedly proclaimed Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja’afar as the “new” Yang Dipertuan Besar at a five-star hotel in Melaka.
Last month, Ismail endorsed a statement by his state executive council that purportedly affirmed Tuanku Muhriz’s removal. The ruler later revoked the appointments of the entire state executive council.

Title: Heavy downpour triggers flash floods across Kuching, roads and Sarawak Plaza basement swamped
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 16 — Several areas in Kuching were hit by flash floods following heavy rain this afternoon.
Flooding was reported at Sarawak Plaza, the Mile 3 underpass, Jalan Tun Jugah and Jalan Batu Lintang after the rain began at around 1.30pm.
The downpour was accompanied by strong winds, with a tree also reportedly uprooted near Wisma Naim here.
Meanwhile, a video posted on Threads, filmed from a restaurant on the basement floor of Sarawak Plaza, showed workers trying to sweep away floodwater.
As of 2.45pm, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) had forecast thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in several parts of Sarawak until 7pm.
The affected areas included Kuching, Samarahan, Serian, Sri Aman, Betong, Mukah, Sarikei, Sibu, Kapit (including Song, Bintulu, Limbang and Miri. — The Borneo Post

Title: Malaysia’s fury rises as Indonesian haze shuts schools, blankets region, and sparks calls for accountability
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — Closed schools, shuttered sports centres and mass mask handouts. Indonesian wildfire haze has caused a regional pollution crisis and prompted growing frustration in neighbours, including Malaysia.
“You need to treat them as an outcast in the region,” Malaysian parliamentarian Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman railed this week talking about the Indonesian fires.
His comments go much further than the gentle diplomatic pressure Malaysia’s government has so far applied, but they reflect a simmering frustration with Indonesia’s inability to control the fires.
“Malaysia and Indonesia are close neighbours, but that relationship must also come with responsibility,” Malaysian parliamentarian Syerleena Abdul Rashid told AFP.
“Why should Malaysians continue paying the price for irresponsible actions beyond our borders?” she said.
Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Thursday defended the approach, saying the South-east Asian nation “has done everything we can” to engage neighbouring Indonesia on the issue.
‘Do the right thing’
But at the popular Batu Caves tourist site, visitors and workers alike expressed frustration.
“You cannot see,” tour operator Diddy Hamidon told AFP, looking out at a vista now shrouded in haze.
“The Indonesian (government) needs to do the right thing,” he added.
Malaysia has been forced to close schools over the haze, and has offered Indonesia help fighting the blazes.
But not until Wednesday did the offer appear to finally have been taken up, after talks involving disaster management officials on both sides, Foreign Minister Mohamad Hasan said.
“The form of cooperation will depend on the outcome of the discussions,” he told local reporters.
“But the authorities of both countries have, for the first time, begun talks on how we can work together to tackle the haze, which appears to be getting worse.”
Indonesia experiences wildfires regularly during its annual dry season, but this year’s blazes have been exacerbated by a strong cycle of the El Nino weather phenomenon, which tends to bring drought to the country.
The fires have burned through hundreds of thousands of hectares in Indonesia and caused air pollution spikes in Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and East Timor, where schools closed this week due to the haze.
Haze shrouds Johor’s skyline across the Causeway, seen from Singapore on October 16, 2026. — AFP pic
The crisis is not the first caused by Indonesian fires, and in 2002, members of the Association of South-east Asian Nations (Asean) inked an agreement on transboundary haze pollution.
But that deal is widely seen as “not worth the paper it’s printed on,” said James Chin, professor of Asian studies at the University of Tasmania.
It has no enforcement mechanism, and previous efforts by Singapore to hold companies linked to wildfires legally culpable have also stalled.
Malaysia has asked Asean for an urgent meeting to discuss the latest crisis, and this year’s summit host Manila confirmed the issue will be on the agenda at a foreign ministers meeting next month.
“Asean members are more than willing to help,” Malaysian parliamentarian Hassan Abdul Karim told AFP, “provided Indonesia is willing to swallow their bigger ego and pride.”
Anger about Indonesia’s inability to control the haze was stoked further by comments over the weekend from Jakarta’s communications agency chief.
“We do not just send smoke... The oxygen in Singapore and Malaysia also comes from our forests,” said Syahganda Nainggolan in a video that swiftly went viral and prompted furious responses.
Syerleena called the remarks “downright insensitive”.
“We value our relationship with Indonesia, but that should not prevent us from speaking up when remarks are inappropriate,” said the parliamentarian.
Indonesia’s President Prabowo Subianto on Monday ordered the government to mobilise maximum efforts to battle wildfires that have been raging for three months in some places.
‘Very, very careful’
The growing public frustration in Malaysia but also neighbouring Singapore, which has topped global major city pollution rankings in recent days, is pressuring governments, said Chin.
But he forecast little progress.
“Asean is very, very careful when it comes to what they call domestic sovereignty. So they are unlikely to do anything,” he said.
Syerleena urged accountability at a regional level, with companies linked to burning held responsible whether they are Indonesian, Malaysian or Singaporean.
“What we need from Jakarta is greater transparency, stronger enforcement against companies responsible for illegal burning, and closer cooperation with neighbouring countries.” — AFP

Title: AAIB releases preliminary report on Long Lellang helicopter crash that killed five
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has published its preliminary report into the September 8 crash of a Flying Doctor Service helicopter at the Long Lellang STOLport in Miri, Sarawak, which killed a pilot and four passengers.
The Transport Ministry said the Bolkow BO105 S helicopter, registered 9M-LLF and operated by Layang-Layang Aerospace Sdn Bhd, was on a scheduled Flying Doctor Service flight from Selungo to the Long Lellang STOLport at the time of the accident.
It said the report compiles the factual information identified at the early stage of the investigation, in line with the government’s commitment to transparency and accountability.
“Investigations are still ongoing to determine the cause and contributing factors of the accident,” the ministry said in a statement today.
It added that the information in the preliminary report is subject to change based on additional evidence, while a full analysis and the investigation’s conclusions will be detailed in the final report.
The ministry stressed that the investigation is aimed at preventing similar accidents, not at apportioning blame or liability to any party.
The investigation is being carried out in accordance with Annex 13 to the Convention on International Civil Aviation and the civil aviation regulations in force.
The ministry expressed its sorrow over the incident and conveyed its condolences to the families of the victims.
It also thanked the AAIB and all parties that assisted in the investigation, and said it remains committed to strengthening the country’s aviation safety.
The preliminary report can be downloaded at https://go.gov.my/Laporan-Insiden-Kemalangan-A11-26.

Title: Khazanah and PNB channelled nearly RM40m into FashionValet in 2018, court hears in Vivy Yusof trial
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 16 — The Sessions Court here was told today that local fashion company, Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd (Fashion Valet), received investment funds totalling nearly RM40 million from Khazanah Nasional Berhad (Khazanah) and Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) eight years ago.
Tay Lay Hong, 54, a banking services manager at the Bukit Damansara branch of Public Bank, said the funds were deposited into a Public Bank account belonging to Fashion Valet through four separate transactions between March and December 2018.
“A review of Fashion Valet’s bank account statements revealed that Khazanah transferred RM7,848,000 on March 23, 2018, and RM11,742,000 on March 26, 2018, while PNB recorded transfers of RM11,953,500 on June 4, 2018, and RM8,364,996 on December 20, 2018,” she said.
The fifth prosecution witness said this in her witness testimony during the trial of Fashion Valet founders Datin Vivy Sofinas Yusof and her husband, Datuk Fadzarudin Shah Anuar, who are facing charges of criminal breach of trust involving RM8 million in investment funds from Khazanah and PNB.
Tay also confirmed that a sum of RM11 million was withdrawn from Fashion Valet’s bank account on August 21, 2018, via an online ‘bulk payment’ transaction.
“This money transfer transaction, amounting to RM11 million, falls under a category of payments requiring verification specifically, approval from an ‘authorised person’ for the Public Bank account held in the name of Fashion Valet Sdn Bhd. However, I am not certain who the authorised person for online banking was.
“To my knowledge, the appointment of an authorised person is based on a Directors’ Resolution; typically, the authorised signatory is the same individual as the authorised person for online banking,” said Tay.
Furthermore, Tay who began her tenure with Public Bank in 1993 said a review of Fadzarudin Shah’s bank statements revealed an incoming transaction of RM5 million on September 4, 2018, from the company 30 Maple Sdn Bhd, with the reference “Interim Dividend”.
“I also reviewed the bank statements for the account held in the name of Vivy Sofinas Yusof, which showed an incoming transaction of RM5 million from 30 Maple Sdn Bhd on September 3, 2018, with the reference ‘CIMB Rentas’,” the witness testified.
According to Tay, a sum of RM5.5 million was withdrawn from each of the couple’s personal accounts at a Public Bank counter on September 5, 2018.
During cross-examination by lawyer Datuk M. Athimulan, the witness confirmed that all information contained in her witness statement was based on documentation, including bank statements.
Additionally, Tay agreed that the RM11 million withdrawn from the Fashion Valet bank account did not necessarily mean the funds were transferred into a single personal account; rather, it involved a ‘bulk’ [transaction]......the ‘payment’ was for items such as staff salaries, shop rental, and so forth.
Vivy, 38, and Fadzarudin, 37, are charged acting with common intention in their capacity as directors of Fashion Valet with criminal breach of trust involving investment funds from Khazanah and PNB. They allegedly authorised payments totalling RM8 million from a Fashion Valet corporate bank account to a company called 30 Maple, without the approval of the Fashion Valet Board of Directors.
The offence was allegedly committed at the Public Bank Berhad branch in Bukit Damansara (located at 36-40 Medan Setia 2, Plaza Damansara, Bukit Damansara) on August 21, 2018 under Section 409 of the Penal Code, read in conjunction with Section 34 of the same Code; if convicted, this carries a penalty of imprisonment for a term of not less than two years and up to 20 years, along with whipping and a potential fine.
They also pleaded not guilty to an alternative charge: acting with common intention to dishonestly misappropriate property belonging to Fashion Valet specifically, the RM8 million in investment funds from Khazanah and PNB at the same location and on the same date.
The couple is charged under Section 403 of the Penal Code, which carries a penalty of imprisonment for a term of not less than six months and up to five years, along with whipping and a mandatory fine, upon conviction.
The trial, presided over by Judge Rosli Ahmad, will resume on November 3. — Bernama

Title: Sarawak gives RM100,000 each to families of Flying Doctor Service crash victims
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 16 — The Sarawak state government has contributed RM100,000 to each of the families of the five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Baram, which occurred on September 8.
Additionally, educational assistance is being provided through Yayasan Sarawak (Sarawak Foundation) to help ease the burden on the victims’ families, specifically by ensuring the continuity of their children’s education.
The contributions were presented by Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg to the next-of-kin of the five victims during a handover ceremony held at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly complex today.
“The loss of a family member cannot be measured in monetary terms, but we can provide some measure of support to them especially to their children.
“Earlier, we presented offer letters from Yayasan Sarawak to assist with the payment of school and university tuition fees for their children,” Abang Johari told reporters following the event.
On September 8, a BO-105 helicopter carrying five individuals, including the pilot, crashed near the Short Take-Off and Landing Port (STOLport) in Long Lellang.
The victims were Alexson Adit Henry, Debra Moset, Dr. Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, Jessie Paya Jok, and Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham. — Bernama

Title: Lawyers urge public to avoid speculation as Zara Qairina inquest heads to January ruling
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Oct 16 — Lawyers involved in the inquest into the death of Zara Qairina Mahathir have urged the public to avoid speculation and allow the judicial process to take its course following the conclusion of witness testimonies.
Lawyer Joan Goh, who represents one of the teenagers accused in the bullying case involving the Form One student, said she hoped the evidence presented during the inquest had been addressed comprehensively.
“We hope there will be no speculation and no unwarranted accusations against anybody, as this remains a tragedy for all the children whose lives have been deeply affected by this case.
“Justice must be guided by evidence and the rule of law, rather than public sentiment or speculation,” Goh told reporters on the sidelines of the proceedings at the Coroner’s Court here today.
Goh also stressed the need to protect the rights, welfare and future of the children involved, urging all parties to respect the legal process and allow them to move forward with their lives.
“The pursuit of justice for Zara must never come at the expense of justice for others, and our thoughts remain with the family over this tragic loss,” she said.
Meanwhile, lawyer Shahlan Jufri, representing Zara Qairina’s mother, said his team had several matters to address in its written submissions, which must be filed by December 15.
He said the coroner had asked all parties to assist the court in identifying discrepancies in witness testimonies and evidence, and to provide their views on the visit conducted at the school.
“The coroner also sought feedback and recommendations from all parties on improving future inquest proceedings, including school safety and investigation procedures,” he said.
Shahlan said his team would review 350 documentary exhibits and more than 5,000 pages of proceedings notes accumulated over the 96-day inquest before filing its submissions.
“We hope the court’s eventual decision will be fair to all parties,” he said.
The Coroner’s Court today fixed January 15 next year to deliver its findings on Zara Qairina’s death.
After 96 days of proceedings, the Coroner’s Court on Wednesday concluded hearing the testimonies of 83 witnesses, including experts, children, teachers and family members.
The inquest began on September 13 last year, with Queen Elizabeth Hospital forensic pathologist Dr Jessie Hiu called as the first witness and investigating officer Insp Wong Yew Zhung as the final witness.
The Attorney-General’s Chambers (AGC) announced on August 13, 2025, that an inquest would be conducted into Zara Qairina’s death after reviewing the investigation report submitted by the police.
The decision followed the exhumation of Zara Qairina’s remains on August 9, 2025, at the Tanjung Ubi Muslim Cemetery in Kampung Mesapol, Sipitang, which was completed at 7.15pm to facilitate a post-mortem examination.
Zara Qairina died at Queen Elizabeth Hospital on July 17, 2025, a day after she was found unconscious near a drain at her school hostel in the early hours of July 16. — Bernama

Title: Police confirm AKPS officer killed in KLIA quarters domestic dispute, knife seized, husband remanded
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 16 — A woman was found dead after allegedly being stabbed by her husband at a Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) quarters unit last night, believed to have stemmed from a domestic dispute.
Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said police received a report regarding the incident at about 9.30pm after a man surrendered himself at the Bandar Baru Salak Tinggi Police Station in Sepang, Selangor, and reported his wife’s death at their residence.
Acting on the information, a police team was dispatched to the scene, where they found a woman, in her 30s, unconscious.
He said initial investigations by the Negeri Sembilan D10 Forensic Division found that the victim sustained injuries suspected to be from being stabbed, while a knife along with several other pieces of evidence were also seized to assist in the investigation.
“The deceased was a customs officer who had been transferred to the Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), effective July 1,” he said in a statement today.
He said a medical team from the Nilai Health Clinic examined the victim at the scene and confirmed her death, and that police have arrested her husband, also in his 30s, to assist in the investigation.
Alzafny said the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder and that the suspect has been remanded for seven days until October 22.
He also advised the public against making any speculation that could interfere with police investigations. — Bernama

Title: China agrees in principle to Malaysia’s proposal for world TVET council, says Zahid
Article:
TIANJIN, Oct 16 — China has agreed in principle to Malaysia’s proposal to establish a World Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Council, said Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Ahmad Zahid said the agreement which includes a proposal for China to serve as the permanent host was conveyed by his counterpart, Ding Xuexiang, and Minister of Education Huai Jinpeng during a meeting yesterday.
He noted that the proposal to establish the World TVET Council, with China acting as the permanent secretariat, was formally presented during his keynote address at the World Technical and Vocational Education and Training Development Conference 2026 (WVTEDC 2026) here today.
“I proposed it yesterday, and today I have officially put it forward in my speech. In terms of principle, Deputy Prime Minister Ding and China’s Minister of Education have agreed,” he said during a press conference following the event.
Ahmad Zahid, who also serves as the Minister of Rural and Regional Development, emphasised that the council is essential for creating a sustainable global platform to foster cooperation in skills development, technology, and workforce training, also expressed confidence in the initiative’s viability, citing China’s experience in organising TVET conferences over the past four years.
Ahmad Zahid, who also chairs the National TVET Committee, added that under this proposal, China would serve as the permanent secretariat to coordinate the sharing of knowledge and expertise within the TVET education ecosystem, thereby enabling member nations to benefit from ongoing collaboration.
The Deputy Prime Minister said the initiative also holds the potential to expand cooperation between TVET institutions in Malaysia and China including a proposed collaboration involving China’s “Luban Workshop” training centers, the Malaysia-China Institute (MCI), and various local TVET institutions.
Ahmad Zahid noted that such cooperation could pave the way for the implementation of skills training programmes, supporting Malaysia’s efforts to develop a highly skilled workforce capable of meeting the demands of the job market.
He added that the participation of over 100 countries and the attendance of 48 ministers at the WVTEDC 2026 conference reflect a global commitment to the development of education and skills training.
“We hope that efforts to strengthen the nation’s TVET ecosystem will continue to receive support from all stakeholders, in line with our aspiration to produce a workforce that meets industry needs, as Malaysia strives to become a highly skilled nation,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Tuanku Muhriz bestows state honours on three Undangs and their consorts
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 16 — The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, conferred the state’s prestigious honours on three Undangs and their consorts at Istana Besar Seri Menanti here yesterday.
The Negeri Sembilan State Secretary’s Office said in a statement today that the three Undangs - Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari of Luak Sungei Ujong, Datuk Mendika Menteri Akhirulzaman Datuk Azrin Khairi of Luak Jelebu and Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid of Luak Rembau — were conferred the Darjah Tertinggi Negeri Sembilan (DTNS).
Their consorts - Tok Puan Sharifah Amirah Ir Syed Ismail Ash-Shahab of Sungei Ujong, Tok Puan Datin Norazizan Mamat of Jelebu and Tok Puan Asmah Yaakob of Rembau - were honoured with the Darjah Mulia Negeri Sembilan (DMNS).
The statement said the DTNS was reserved for the four Undangs and the Tunku Besar Tampin, while the DMNS was reserved for their consorts.
Also present at the ceremony were the Tunku Ampuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Aishah Rohani Tengku Besar Mahmud, Tunku Besar Seri Menanti Tunku Ali Redhauddin Tuanku Muhriz, and Tunku Panglima Besar Tunku Zain Al-‘Abidin.
Other attendees included State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim, State Legal Adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal and State Financial Officer Datuk Masri Razali. — Bernama
